definition_zh: 老板；上司；负责人；（口语）指挥、摆布
definition_en: the person who employs you or is in charge of you, or to tell people what to do in a pushy way
core_image: 车间里站在图纸旁安排工作的人
scene: 车间一早开工，负责人站在图纸旁，把当天的任务分给每个人。The boss gave each worker a task for the day.
sceneCN: 这里 boss 是「负责人；上司」（第 1 个义项：管事的雇主或上级）；句意为负责人给每位工人分配了当天的任务。

pos.zh: 名词：老板；上司；负责人
动词：指挥；摆布；对……发号施令

derivatives.zh: 由 boss 加 -y 构成，义为「专横的；爱发号施令的」
由 bossy 加 -ness 构成，义为「专横；爱指挥别人」
由 boss 加 -less 构成，义为「没有上司的；无人管理的」

senses.title: The person in charge
senses.definition: the person who employs workers or directs them in a job
senses.definitionCN: 雇用工人或在工作中指挥工人的人
senses.example: My boss asked me to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 我的老板让我完成这份报告。
senses.why: The word came from Dutch baas, meaning master, and American workers used it for the man who hired them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自荷兰语 baas，意为「主人」，美国工人用它称呼雇用自己的人。

senses.title: The head of a group
senses.definition: the person who leads a team, office or organization
senses.definitionCN: 领导团队、办公室或机构的人
senses.example: She is the boss of the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 她是整个部门的负责人。
senses.why: From the workplace the word spread to any group with a leader, because every group needs someone in charge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从工作场所扩展到任何有领导者的群体，因为每个群体都需要一个管事的人。

senses.title: To order people about
senses.definition: to tell people what to do in a pushy or unfair way
senses.definitionCN: 以强势或不公平的方式叫人做事
senses.example: He likes to boss the younger players around.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢对年轻队员呼来喝去。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, and it kept the pushy tone of someone giving orders without being asked.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，保留了一个人未经邀请就发号施令的强势口气。

intro.en: Boss came into American English from Dutch, and it has moved from master to any kind of leader.
intro.cn: boss 从荷兰语进入美式英语，并从「主人」扩展到任何领导者。

items.en: Dutch baas meant master or head, a word used by tradesmen and sailors.
items.cn: 荷兰语 baas 意为主人或头领，是商人与水手常用的词。

items.en: American English borrowed boss in the nineteenth century, first for the man who hired labour.
items.cn: 美式英语在十九世纪借入 boss，最初指雇用劳工的人。

items.en: From the workshop and the docks the word spread to offices and every kind of employer.
items.cn: 从车间与码头，这个词扩展到办公室与各类雇主。

items.en: In the twentieth century boss became a verb meaning to give orders in a pushy way.
items.cn: 二十世纪 boss 又变成动词，表示以强势方式发号施令。

items.en: Today boss means any person in charge, and the verb still carries a critical tone.
items.cn: 今天 boss 指任何负责人，动词用法仍带批评口气。

note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音接近的词；近义组收工作场合的其他领导者称呼。

entries.definition: A person who controls a business or part of one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经理」，指管理企业或其一部分的人。

root: boss 来自荷兰语 baas，意为主人或头领，美式英语在十九世纪借入，最初指雇用劳工的人。这个词从车间与码头扩展到办公室和各类雇主，随后又变成动词，表示以强势方式发号施令。今天 boss 指任何负责人，动词用法仍带批评口气。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of boss rest on one picture: a person standing over the work and telling others what to do.
sensesIntro.cn: boss 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个人站在工作上方，吩咐别人怎么做。

core.cn: 核心意象：站在工作图旁分发任务的人

branches.en: THE EMPLOYER: the person who hires and directs workers is the first sense.
branches.cn: 雇主线：雇用并指挥工人的人是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE LEADER: any head of a group can be called boss.
branches.cn: 领导线：任何群体的头儿都可以叫 boss。

branches.en: THE ORDER: the verb keeps the pushy way of giving orders.
branches.cn: 命令线：动词保留了强势发号施令的方式。

branches.en: THE CHARGE: employer and group leader both mean being in charge.
branches.cn: 负责线：雇主与群体领导者都表示「管事」。

branches.en: THE TONE: the leader and the pushy verb share one voice.
branches.cn: 口气线：领导者与强势动词共享同一种口气。

definition_zh: 两者都；双方；两个（都）；（both...and...）既……又……
definition_en: used to talk about two people or things together, not just one of them
core_image: 两只手同时举着两个苹果
scene: 孩子两只手各拿一个苹果，笑着举起来给妈妈看。Both children held an apple in each hand.
sceneCN: 这里 both 是「两者都」（第 1 个义项：两个一起、不只有其中一个）；句意为两个孩子每人手里都拿着一个苹果。

pos.zh: 限定词：两个都；双方
代词：两者；双方
连词：既……又……（与 and 连用）

derivatives.zh: 常与 both 对照：两者中的任意一个
常与 both 对照：两者都不

senses.title: The two together
senses.definition: used before a noun to include two people or things, not only one
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，把两个人或物一起包括进来，而不只是其中一个
senses.example: Both children were asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 两个孩子都睡着了。
senses.why: Old English had a word for the two together, and both keeps that sense of a complete pair.
senses.whyCN: 古英语有一个表示「两者一起」的词，both 保留了「一整对」的意思。

senses.title: The two as pronouns
senses.definition: used as a pronoun, usually with of, to stand for two people or things already known
senses.definitionCN: 作代词，常与 of 连用，指已经提到的两个人或物
senses.example: She invited both of them.
senses.exampleCN: 她把他们两个都邀请了。
senses.why: When the noun is already known, the word can stand alone as a pronoun and still point at the pair.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已经知道时，这个词可以单独作代词，仍指向那一对。

senses.title: Both ... and ...
senses.definition: used with and to join two qualities or actions and give equal weight to each
senses.definitionCN: 与 and 连用，连接两种性质或动作，使两者份量相同
senses.example: She is both kind and honest.
senses.exampleCN: 她既善良又诚实。
senses.why: The pair sense works for qualities too: both ... and ... says the two joined items count equally.
senses.whyCN: 「一对」的意思也适用于性质：both ... and ... 表示所连的两项同等重要。

intro.en: Both descends from an old English phrase for the two together, with a Norse form shaping its modern spelling.
intro.cn: both 源自古英语表示「那两个一起」的说法，北欧语形式又塑造了它的现代拼写。

items.en: Old English ba tha meant both those, joining a word for both with a word for those.
items.cn: 古英语 ba tha 意为「那两个都」，把表示「两者」的词与表示「那些」的词连在一起。

items.en: Old Norse badir, meaning both, reshaped the word during the Viking age.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 badir 意为「两者」，在维京时期重塑了这个词。

items.en: Middle English settled on the short form both for a complete pair.
items.cn: 中古英语定下短形式 both，用于完整的一对。

items.en: Grammarians described both as a determiner and a pronoun that always looks at two.
items.cn: 语法学家把 both 描述为始终指向两个的限定词与代词。

items.en: Today both also pairs with and to give two items equal weight.
items.cn: 今天 both 还与 and 搭配，使两项获得同等份量。

definition_zh: 打扰；使烦恼；费心；麻烦（名词）
definition_en: to annoy or worry someone, to make an effort, or a troublesome thing
core_image: 正在专心写字时，一只手在你肩上拍了一下
scene: 孩子正专心写作业，弟弟在门口大声喊他，他只好放下笔。The noise bothered him while he was studying.
sceneCN: 这里 bother 是「打扰；使烦恼」（第 1 个义项：打断别人并让其不快）；句意为学习时那声音打扰了他。

pos.zh: 动词：打扰；使烦恼；费心
名词：麻烦；令人烦恼的事

derivatives.zh: 由 bother 加 -some 构成，义为「令人烦恼的；讨厌的」
由 un- 与 bothered 构成，义为「不受打扰的；不在意的」
由 bother 加 -ation 构成，义为「麻烦；恼人的事」，也用作感叹

senses.title: To interrupt and disturb
senses.definition: to interrupt someone who is busy, or to disturb them with noise and questions
senses.definitionCN: 打断正在忙的人，或用噪音和问话干扰他
senses.example: Sorry to bother you at this hour.
senses.exampleCN: 抱歉在这个时间打扰你。
senses.why: Bother first meant to deafen or buzz in the ear, so interrupting someone grew from that noisy picture.
senses.whyCN: bother 最初有「震耳、在耳边嗡嗡响」的意思，所以「打扰」是从那幅吵闹的画面长出来的。

senses.title: To worry or upset
senses.definition: to make someone feel annoyed, worried or uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到恼火、担心或不舒服
senses.example: The noise bothered the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪音让邻居们很烦。
senses.why: The same disturbance can land inside a person as worry, so the verb also means to upset someone.
senses.whyCN: 同样的干扰也可以落在人心里变成担忧，所以这个动词也指使人心烦。

senses.title: To take the trouble
senses.definition: to make an effort to do something, usually used in questions and negatives
senses.definitionCN: 花力气去做某事，常用于疑问句和否定句
senses.example: Don't bother waiting for me.
senses.exampleCN: 不用费心等我了。
senses.why: If a task is a bother, then bothering to do it means accepting the trouble it costs.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事本身就是麻烦，那么 bothering to do it 就是接受它为这事付出的麻烦。

senses.title: A troublesome thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that causes trouble or extra effort
senses.definitionCN: 带来麻烦或额外费力的人或事
senses.example: Filling in these forms is a real bother.
senses.exampleCN: 填这些表格真是件麻烦事。
senses.why: The verb became a noun, so the trouble itself is simply called a bother.
senses.whyCN: 动词变成名词，于是麻烦本身就直接被叫作 a bother。

intro.en: Bother is a fairly young word, first recorded in the eighteenth century, and its deeper origin is not certain.
intro.cn: bother 是相当年轻的词，最早记录于十八世纪，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Bother appears in English writing in the eighteenth century, first as a word for noisy disturbance.
items.cn: bother 在十八世纪的英语文献中出现，最初指吵闹的干扰。

items.en: Some scholars connect it with a dialect word meaning to buzz or deafen, but the link is not proved.
items.cn: 有学者把它与一个表示嗡嗡响或震耳的方言词联系起来，但这条线并未得到证实。

items.en: No old Germanic or Latin root can be securely traced, so the deeper history stays uncertain.
items.cn: 无法可靠追溯到古老的日耳曼语或拉丁语词根，所以更早的历史仍不确定。

items.en: From disturbance the verb spread to worry, to effort and finally to the noun meaning trouble.
items.cn: 从「干扰」出发，这个动词扩展到担心、费力，最后又产生名词「麻烦」。

items.en: Today bother covers interruption, worry, effort and a troublesome task.
items.cn: 今天 bother 覆盖打断、担心、费力与恼人的事情。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words about disturbing and annoying.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收与打扰、烦恼有关的词。

entries.definition: A problem or something that causes extra effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「麻烦」，对应 bother 的名词义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Bother is first recorded in the eighteenth century, and its deeper root is uncertain.
normal.cn: bother 最早记录于十八世纪，更早的词根并不确定。

normal.en: It began with noisy disturbance, which is why it suits interruptions so well.
normal.cn: 它从吵闹的干扰开始，所以特别适合表示「打断」。

normal.en: If a task is a bother, bothering to do it means accepting the trouble.
normal.cn: 如果一件事本身就是麻烦，bothering to do it 就是接受这份麻烦。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with sorry, don't, about and someone.
normal.cn: 它常与 sorry、don't、about、someone 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-t-h-e-r; the th is voiced, as in this.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-t-h-e-r，th 读作浊音，就像 this 里的音。

abstract.en: See a hand tap your shoulder while you are writing: that tap is bother.
abstract.cn: 想象你正在写字时，一只手在你肩上拍了一下：那一拍就是 bother。

abstract.en: Let the tap become a buzzing sound that stays in the ear, and the word deepens.
abstract.cn: 让那一拍变成耳边挥之不去的嗡嗡声，这个词的意思就加深了。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the tapping hand bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那只拍肩的手把意思带回来。

examples.en: Sorry to bother you at this hour.
examples.cn: 抱歉在这个时间打扰你。

examples.en: The noise bothered the neighbours.
examples.cn: 那噪音让邻居们很烦。

examples.en: Don't bother waiting for me.
examples.cn: 不用费心等我了。

root: bother 是十八世纪才出现在英语中的年轻词，最初指吵闹的干扰；有学者把它与表示嗡嗡响或震耳的方言词联系起来，但这条线未获证实，更早的词根无法可靠追溯。由「干扰」出发，它扩展到担心、费力，最后又产生名词「麻烦」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bother rest on one picture: something noisy or sudden landing on a person who is busy.
sensesIntro.cn: bother 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：某种吵闹或突然的东西，落在正忙的人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tapping your shoulder while you write
core.cn: 核心意象：你写字时肩上被拍了一下

branches.en: THE INTERRUPTION: disturbing a busy person is the first sense.
branches.cn: 打断线：干扰一个正在忙的人，是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE WORRY: the same disturbance lands inside as upset.
branches.cn: 担心线：同样的干扰落在心里变成不快。

branches.en: THE EFFORT: accepting a task's trouble is also called bothering.
branches.cn: 费力线：接受一件事的麻烦，也叫 bothering。

branches.en: THE NUISANCE: the noun names the troublesome thing itself.
branches.cn: 麻烦线：名词指的就是那件恼人的事。

branches.en: THE DISTURBANCE: an outside noise and an inner upset share one image.
branches.cn: 干扰线：外面的噪音与心里的不快共享同一幅画面。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vexare 与 molestare 是有记录的「使人烦恼」动词，它们是平行词，不是 bother 的来源。

definition_zh: 瓶子；一瓶（的量）；把……装瓶；奶瓶
definition_en: a tall container with a narrow neck for holding liquid, or to put liquid into such a container
core_image: 窄颈玻璃瓶里装着清水，瓶口塞着软木塞
scene: 餐桌上放着一只窄颈玻璃瓶，里面是清水，瓶口塞着一只软木塞。He filled the bottle with cold water.
sceneCN: 这里 bottle 是「瓶子」（第 1 个义项：盛液体的容器）；句意为他往瓶子里装满了凉水。

pos.zh: 名词：瓶子；一瓶（的量）；奶瓶
动词：把……装瓶；用奶瓶喂养

derivatives.zh: 由 bottle 加 -ed 构成，义为「瓶装的」

senses.title: A narrow-necked container
senses.definition: a tall container with a narrow neck, used for holding liquids
senses.definitionCN: 高而颈窄、用来盛放液体的容器
senses.example: She put the milk in a glass bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 她把牛奶装进一只玻璃瓶。
senses.why: Old French bouteille named a flask, and the narrow-necked shape is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 bouteille 指细颈瓶，窄颈的形状至今仍是这个词的核心。

senses.title: The amount inside one
senses.definition: the amount of liquid that one bottle holds
senses.definitionCN: 一只瓶子所能装下的液体的量
senses.example: They drank a whole bottle of juice.
senses.exampleCN: 他们喝了一整瓶果汁。
senses.why: A container can stand for its contents, so a bottle also measures how much it holds.
senses.whyCN: 容器可以代指其中的内容，所以 a bottle 也用来量它装了多少。

senses.title: To put into bottles
senses.definition: to put a liquid into bottles for storing or selling
senses.definitionCN: 把液体装入瓶中以便保存或出售
senses.example: They bottle the wine on the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在农场把葡萄酒装瓶。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to do what a bottle does, which is to hold and preserve a liquid.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：做瓶子所做的事，也就是盛装并保存液体。

intro.en: Bottle came through French from a Latin word for a cask, and the shape has stayed narrow-necked for centuries.
intro.cn: bottle 经法语来自拉丁语中表示「木桶」的词，几个世纪以来都保持窄颈形状。

items.en: Late Latin buttis meant a cask or a barrel, the container behind the whole family.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 buttis 指木桶或大桶，是整个词族背后的容器。

items.en: A small cask was called butticula, and that word named a flask rather than a barrel.
items.cn: 小桶被叫作 butticula，这个词指的是细颈瓶而不是大桶。

items.en: Old French bouteille carried the flask sense into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 bouteille 把这个「细颈瓶」的意思带进日常使用。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word, and the modern spelling settled as bottle.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个词，现代拼写最终定为 bottle。

items.en: Today bottle also measures liquid, and the verb means to fill or preserve in bottles.
items.cn: 今天 bottle 也用来量液体，动词则表示装瓶或瓶装保存。

definition_zh: 底部；底端；最下层；尽头；臀部
definition_en: the lowest part of something, the least important position, or the far end
core_image: 一池清水，视线一直落到池底的石子
scene: 池塘的水很清，站在岸边能看见池底的白色石子。You can see the stones at the bottom of the pond.
sceneCN: 这里 bottom 是「底部」（第 1 个义项：物体最低的那一面）；句意为你能看见池塘底部的石子。

pos.zh: 名词：底部；底端；最下层；臀部
形容词：最下面的；最低的

derivatives.zh: 由 bottom 加 -less 构成，义为「无底的；深不可测的」
由 bottom 加 -most 构成，义为「最底下的」
由 bottom 与 up 组合而成，义为「自下而上的」

senses.title: The lowest part
senses.definition: the lowest or deepest part of a container, surface or object
senses.definitionCN: 容器、表面或物体最低、最深的部分
senses.example: The keys were at the bottom of the bag.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙在包的底部。
senses.why: Old English botm meant the ground or the lowest part, and that physical sense is still the centre.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 botm 指地面或最低处，这个身体层面的义项仍是中心。

senses.title: The lowest position
senses.definition: the least important or lowest position in a group or scale
senses.definitionCN: 群体或等级中地位最低、最不重要的位置
senses.example: The team finished at the bottom of the league.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在联赛中排名垫底。
senses.why: A ladder and a table both have a bottom, so the lowest rank in a group is pictured the same way.
senses.whyCN: 梯子和表格都有底部，于是一个群体中最低的等级也被这样描画。

senses.title: The far end
senses.definition: the far end of a long place, such as a garden, street or page
senses.definitionCN: 狭长地方最远的一端，如花园、街道或页面的末端
senses.example: There is a shed at the bottom of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 花园尽头有一间小屋。
senses.why: When you look along a long space, its far end sits at the limit of your view, as if at the bottom of the picture.
senses.whyCN: 沿着狭长空间望去，最远的一端落在视野的边界，好像画面底部一样。

senses.title: The part you sit on
senses.definition: the part of the body that you sit on, used in a polite or slightly informal way
senses.definitionCN: 坐着时承重的那部分身体，用于礼貌或略口语的说法
senses.example: The fall hurt his bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 那一跤摔疼了他的屁股。
senses.why: The lowest part of the body took the same word, softened so that it can be said without embarrassment.
senses.whyCN: 身体最低的部分也用了同一个词，语气 softened 之后可以不必尴尬地说出口。

intro.en: Bottom is an old word for the ground and the lowest part of anything, and English extended it to rank and to the body.
intro.cn: bottom 是表示地面与最低处的古词，英语把它扩展到等级与身体。

items.en: Old English botm meant the lowest part, the ground, or the bed of the sea.
items.cn: 古英语 botm 指最低处、地面或海底。

items.en: German Boden and Dutch bodem are relatives, all meaning ground or floor.
items.cn: 德语 Boden 与荷兰语 bodem 是同源词，都表示地面或底部。

items.en: Because a scale is pictured as a vertical stack, the lowest rank became the bottom.
items.cn: 由于等级被想象成竖着堆叠，最低的等级就成了 the bottom。

items.en: The lowest part of the body borrowed the word in a softened way.
items.cn: 身体最低的部分以委婉的方式借用了这个词。

items.en: Today bottom covers the base of things, the lowest rank, the far end of a place and the body part.

definition_zh: 碗；一碗（的量）；碗状物；投球（板球）
definition_en: a round deep dish for food, the amount it holds, or something shaped like it
core_image: 一只圆口深碗，碗里盛着热气腾腾的米饭
scene: 餐桌上摆着一只厚实的陶瓷碗，里面盛满热米饭，白气正往上飘。She filled the bowl with hot rice.
sceneCN: 这里 bowl 是「碗」（第 1 个义项：圆而深的盛食器皿）；句意为她把热米饭盛满了一碗。

pos.zh: 名词：碗；一碗（的量）；碗状物
动词：投球（板球）；滚动

senses.title: The deep round dish
senses.definition: a round, deep dish used for soup, rice or other food
senses.definitionCN: 圆而深、用来盛汤、米饭或其他食物的器皿
senses.example: She filled the bowl with hot rice.
senses.exampleCN: 她把热米饭盛满了一碗。
senses.why: Old English bolla named a round pot or cup, and the round hollow shape is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bolla 指圆形锅或杯，圆而中空的形状至今仍是这个词的核心。

senses.title: The amount it holds
senses.definition: the amount of food that one bowl contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只碗所能盛放的食物量
senses.example: He ate two bowls of noodles.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃了两碗面。
senses.why: A dish can stand for what is in it, so a bowl also measures a serving of food.
senses.whyCN: 器皿可以代指其中的东西，所以 a bowl 也用来量一份食物。

senses.title: Anything bowl-shaped
senses.definition: a thing with a round hollow shape, such as a stadium or the part of a pipe
senses.definitionCN: 具有圆而中空形状的东西，如体育场或烟斗的斗
senses.example: The concert was held in a huge bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会在一个巨大的碗形场地举行。
senses.why: The dish's round hollow form was applied to stadiums and other hollow things, so the shape itself took the name.
senses.whyCN: 碗的圆而中空的外形被用于体育场等中空事物，于是形状本身得了这个名字。

senses.title: To send the ball
senses.definition: to throw the ball towards the batsman in cricket
senses.definitionCN: 在板球中把球投向击球手
senses.example: He bowled the first ball of the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他投出了比赛的第一球。
senses.why: In cricket the ball is sent along the ground much as a bowl rolls, so the verb borrowed the round movement.
senses.whyCN: 板球里球沿着地面送出，很像碗在滚动，于是动词借用了这种圆形的运动。

intro.en: Bowl began as a word for a round pot, and its round hollow form has been applied to many things since.
intro.cn: bowl 最初指圆形锅，它圆而中空的外形此后被应用到许多事物上。

items.en: Old English bolla meant a round pot or cup, a vessel for food and drink.
items.cn: 古英语 bolla 指圆形锅或杯，是盛食物与饮料的器皿。

items.en: German Bowle and Dutch bol are relatives, all naming something round and hollow.
items.cn: 德语 Bowle 与荷兰语 bol 是同源词，都指圆而中空的东西。

items.en: Because the dish is round and hollow, English called any such hollow form a bowl.
items.cn: 由于这种器皿圆而中空，英语把任何类似的中空形状都叫 bowl。

items.en: Cricket used the rolling motion of a bowl for the act of sending the ball.
items.cn: 板球借用了碗滚动般的运动，来表示把球送出去的动作。

items.en: Today bowl covers the dish, its contents, bowl-shaped things and the cricket verb.
items.cn: 今天 bowl 覆盖碗、碗中之量、碗状物以及板球动词。

root: bowl 来自古英语 bolla，指圆形锅或杯，德语 Bowle 与荷兰语 bol 是同源词，都指圆而中空的东西。由于这种器皿的圆而中空，英语把任何类似的中空形状也叫 bowl；器皿又可代指其中的食物，于是有了「一碗之量」。板球借用了碗滚动般的运动，用来表示投球。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bowl rest on one picture: a round hollow curve that can hold food, measure it, be enlarged into a stadium, or roll a ball.
sensesIntro.cn: bowl 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：一条圆而中空的弧线，它可以盛食物、量食物、放大成体育场，也可以滚动一只球。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只厚实陶瓷碗盛满热米饭

branches.cn: 器皿线：圆而深的容器是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the dish stands for the food it holds.
branches.cn: 计量线：器皿代指它所盛的食物。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: any round hollow form can take the name.
branches.cn: 形状线：任何圆而中空的形状都能得到这个名字。

branches.en: THE ROLL: cricket borrowed the rolling curve for sending the ball.
branches.cn: 滚动线：板球借用这条滚动弧线来表示投球。

branches.cn: 份量线：器皿与一份食物共享同一条弧线。

definition_zh: 箱子；盒子；一盒（的量）；方框；拳击
definition_en: a container with straight sides, the amount it holds, a square space on a form, or to fight with the fists
core_image: 一个方方正正的纸箱，盖子正被打开
scene: 快递员把方方正正的纸箱放在门口，孩子蹲下去掀开箱盖。The box was full of books.
sceneCN: 这里 box 是「箱子；盒子」（第 1 个义项：方正的容器）；句意为这个箱子里装满了书。

pos.zh: 名词：箱子；盒子；方框
动词：拳击；把……装箱

derivatives.zh: 由 box 加 -ing 构成，义为「拳击」
由 box 加 -er 构成，义为「拳击手」，也指拳师犬
由 box 加 -ful 构成，义为「一盒之量」
由 box 加 -y 构成，义为「箱形的；方方正正的」

senses.title: The straight-sided container
senses.definition: a container with flat sides, usually with a lid, used for holding or carrying things
senses.definitionCN: 有平直侧面、通常带盖、用来装盛或搬运东西的容器
senses.example: The box was full of books.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子里装满了书。
senses.why: The container word came through Latin from Greek pyxis, a box, and the straight-sided shape has stayed.
senses.whyCN: 这个容器词经拉丁语来自希腊语 pyxis（盒子），方正的外形一直保留。

senses.title: The amount it holds
senses.definition: the amount of something that one box contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只盒子所能装下的某物的量
senses.example: She bought a box of eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一盒鸡蛋。
senses.why: A container can stand for its contents, so a box also measures what is inside it.
senses.whyCN: 容器可以代指内容，所以 a box 也用来量里面的东西。

senses.title: A square on a form
senses.definition: a square space on a form or page where you write or mark something
senses.definitionCN: 表格或页面上用来填写或标记的方形空格
senses.example: Tick the box next to your name.
senses.exampleCN: 在你名字旁边的方框里打勾。
senses.why: A printed square looks like the top of a box, so the marked space on a form took the same word.
senses.whyCN: 印刷的方格看起来像盒子的顶面，于是表格上要标记的空格也用了同一个词。

senses.title: To fight with fists
senses.definition: to fight someone with your fists, wearing thick gloves in the sport
senses.definitionCN: 用拳头与人搏斗，在运动中戴厚手套
senses.example: He learned to box when he was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 他十岁时学的拳击。
senses.why: The verb may come from the raised fists meeting like two boxes, a separate line from the container word.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可能来自两只举起的拳头像两个盒子相撞，与容器义是另一条线。

intro.en: Box has two histories that look alike: the container came from Greek, while the fighting verb has its own uncertain path.
intro.cn: box 有两条看起来相似的历史：容器义来自希腊语，而拳击动词走的是另一条不确定的路。

items.en: Greek pyxis meant a box, especially a small one for medicines or jewels.
items.cn: 希腊语 pyxis 指盒子，尤其是装药或珠宝的小盒。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as buxis, and the word passed into English as box.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 buxis，这个词随后进入英语成为 box。

items.en: Because a box holds things, the word also came to mean the amount it contains.
items.cn: 由于盒子能装东西，这个词也用来表示它所装的量。

items.en: The square space on a printed form was named after the box's flat top.
items.cn: 印刷表格上的方形空格因盒子的平顶而得名。

items.en: The verb meaning to fight with fists appeared later, and its origin is not certain.
items.cn: 表示用拳头搏斗的动词出现较晚，来源并不确定。

definition_en: a male child or young man, or a son
core_image: 操场上抱着球跑过来的小男孩

pos.zh: 名词：男孩；儿子；男青年

senses.title: A male child
senses.definition: a male child, or a young man who is not yet fully grown
senses.definitionCN: 男性儿童，或尚未完全成年的年轻男性
senses.example: A boy ran across the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 一个男孩跑过操场。
senses.why: Middle English boi named a male child, and that everyday sense is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 boi 指男性儿童，这个日常义项仍是词义的中心。

senses.title: A son
senses.definition: a son of a parent, used when speaking about a family
senses.definitionCN: 父母的孩子，用于谈论家庭时
senses.example: They have two boys and one girl.
senses.exampleCN: 他们有两个儿子和一个女儿。
senses.why: A family speaking of its male child says my boy, so the word also means son.
senses.whyCN: 家庭提到自己的男性孩子时会说 my boy，于是这个词也指儿子。

senses.title: A fellow, in casual speech
senses.definition: used informally for a man or a friend, often in friendly address
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指某个男人或朋友，常用于友好的称呼
senses.example: Good luck, old boy.
senses.exampleCN: 祝你好运，老兄。
senses.why: The word for a young male softened into a friendly way of addressing any man.
senses.whyCN: 原本指年轻男性的词语气变轻，成了称呼任何男性的友好说法。

intro.en: Boy is a Middle English word of uncertain origin, and it may have begun as a name for a servant.
intro.cn: boy 是中古英语词，来源不确定，最初可能指仆役。

items.en: Middle English boi first appears with the sense of a male servant or a low-ranking man.
items.cn: 中古英语 boi 最初出现时指男仆或地位低的男子。

items.en: No old Germanic or Latin root can be securely traced, so the deeper origin stays unknown.
items.cn: 无法可靠追溯到古老的日耳曼语或拉丁语词根，所以更早的来源仍属未知。

items.en: By the late Middle Ages the word had moved to its main modern sense, a male child.
items.cn: 到中古英语晚期，这个词已转向今天的主要义项：男性儿童。

items.en: Parents used it for their sons, which is how boy also came to mean son.
items.cn: 父母用它称呼自己的儿子，boy 由此也指儿子。

items.en: Today boy means a male child, a son, or a friendly word for a man.
items.cn: 今天 boy 指男孩、儿子，或对男性的友好称呼。

normal.en: Middle English boi first meant a male servant, and later a male child.
normal.cn: 中古英语 boi 最初指男仆，后来指男性儿童。

normal.en: No old root can be traced with certainty, so the deeper history stays open.
normal.cn: 无法确定追溯更古老的词根，所以更早的历史仍是开放的。

normal.en: Parents said my boy for a son, which is how the family sense grew.
normal.cn: 父母用 my boy 称呼儿子，家属义就是这样长出来的。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with little, school, band and old.
normal.cn: 它常与 little、school、band、old 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-y; the oy sounds like the oi in coin.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-y，中间的 oy 读得像 coin 里的 oi。

abstract.en: See a small figure running with a ball, one shoelace loose: that is a boy.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小小的身影抱着球跑，一根鞋带松着：那就是 boy。

abstract.en: Let the same figure grow older and the word can become a friendly old boy.
abstract.cn: 让同一个身影长大，这个词就能变成友好的 old boy。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the running figure bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那个奔跑的身影把意思带回来。

examples.en: A boy ran across the playground.
examples.cn: 一个男孩跑过操场。

examples.en: They have two boys and one girl.
examples.cn: 他们有两个儿子和一个女儿。

examples.en: Good luck, old boy.
examples.cn: 祝你好运，老兄。

root: boy 来自中古英语 boi，最初指男仆或地位低的男子，更早的词根无法可靠追溯。到中古英语晚期，它转向今天的主要义项「男性儿童」；父母用 my boy 称呼儿子，于是又有了「儿子」的意思。今天这个词还可作对男性的友好称呼。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of boy rest on one picture: a young male figure, who can be a child, a son, or a familiar old friend.
sensesIntro.cn: boy 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个年轻的男性身影，他可以是孩子、儿子，也可以是熟悉的老伙计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small figure running with a ball, one shoelace loose
core.cn: 核心意象：抱着球奔跑的小身影，一根鞋带松着

branches.en: THE CHILD: a male child is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 儿童线：男性儿童是今天最核心的义项。

branches.en: THE SON: parents use the word for their male child.
branches.cn: 儿子线：父母用这个词称呼自己的男性孩子。

branches.en: THE FELLOW: the word softened into a friendly way to address a man.
branches.cn: 家伙线：这个词语气变轻，成了对男性的友好称呼。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the child and the son are one person seen at home.
branches.cn: 家庭线：孩子与儿子是同一个人从家庭角度看。

branches.en: THE ADDRESS: from a young male to any familiar man.
branches.cn: 称呼线：从年轻男性扩展到任何熟悉的男性。

definition_zh: 大脑；头脑、智力；聪明人、主脑；（口语）猛击头部
definition_en: the organ inside the head that controls thought and feeling, the ability to think, or the clever person who plans for a group
core_image: 颅骨里一团掌管思考与记忆的灰白组织
scene: 生物课上，老师指着人体模型说，这团组织让人会思考、会记忆。The teacher pointed at the model and said the brain controls thought and memory.
sceneCN: 这里 brain 是「大脑」（第 1 个义项：颅腔内主管思维与感觉的器官）；句意为老师指着模型说，大脑控制思维与记忆。

pos.zh: 名词：大脑；头脑；智力；聪明人
动词：（口语）猛击……的头部

derivatives.zh: 由 brain 加 -y 构成，义为「聪明的；有头脑的」
由 brain 加 -less 构成，义为「没头脑的；愚蠢的」
由 brain 与 storm 组合而成，义为「头脑风暴；突然想到的好主意」

senses.title: The organ inside the head
senses.definition: the organ inside the skull that controls thought, memory and feeling
senses.definitionCN: 颅腔内控制思维、记忆与感觉的器官
senses.example: The brain needs oxygen to work well.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑需要氧气才能正常工作。
senses.why: Old English braegen named the soft tissue inside the skull, and this physical sense is still the base of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 braegen 指颅骨内那团柔软的组织，这个实体义至今仍是整个词义的根基。

senses.title: The power to think
senses.definition: the ability to think, learn and understand things
senses.definitionCN: 思考、学习与理解事物的能力
senses.example: It takes brains to solve this puzzle.
senses.exampleCN: 解开这个谜题需要动脑子。
senses.why: Because the organ does the thinking, the word slipped from the flesh to the power that the flesh gives.
senses.whyCN: 因为这团组织负责思考，词义便从肉体本身滑向它带来的思维能力。

senses.title: The clever planner
senses.definition: the most intelligent person in a group, who plans what the others do
senses.definitionCN: 群体中最聪明、为其他人出谋划策的人
senses.example: She is the brains behind the new app.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这款新应用的幕后主脑。
senses.why: A group names its thinker its brain, taking the whole person from the one part that plans the work.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体把出主意的人称作它的 brain，用负责筹划的那一部分来代指整个人。

senses.title: To hit on the head
senses.definition: to hit someone hard on the head, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口头上指用力击打某人的头部
senses.example: The falling branch brained the careless walker.
senses.exampleCN: 落下的树枝重重砸中了那个不小心的行人。
senses.why: The noun turned into a joke verb: the brain is the target, so hitting the head is to brain someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了带玩笑口气的动词：脑子是受击的部位，所以打头就说成 brain 某人。

intro.en: Brain is an old Germanic word for the tissue inside the skull, and its meaning widened from flesh to thought.
intro.cn: brain 是日耳曼语中表示颅腔内组织的古老词，词义从肉体扩展到思维。

items.en: Braegen named the soft tissue inside the skull and is the oldest recorded form of the word.
items.cn: braegen 指颅骨内的柔软组织，是这个词有记录的最古老形式。

items.en: Dutch and German still have close words for the same organ, which points to one common root.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语中仍有指同一器官的近亲词，说明它们来自同一个词根。

items.en: The spelling settled as brain, and the word stayed firmly tied to the organ.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 brain，词义仍牢牢系在这个器官上。

items.en: Since the organ does the thinking, the word also came to mean the power to think.
items.cn: 由于这团组织负责思考，这个词又引申为思考的能力。

items.en: Today brain covers the organ, the mind and the clever planner, and it keeps a joking verb.
items.cn: 今天 brain 兼指器官、头脑与聪明的主脑，还保留了一个玩笑式的动词用法。

abstract.en: Let the knot glow and the same picture turns into the power to think.

branches.cn: 器官线：颅内的那团组织是最字面的第一个义项。

definition_en: a product name or mark that identifies a company's goods, a particular type of something, a mark burned on skin, or to mark and label someone in a fixed way
core_image: 烧红的铁印压在木箱或牲畜身上留下的记号
scene: 牧场上，农人用烧红的铁印在牛身上留下记号，表示它归谁所有。The farmer pressed a hot iron brand onto the cow's hide.
sceneCN: 这里 brand 是「烙印」（第 3 个义项：用烧红铁器留下的标记）；句意为农人用烧红的铁印在牛身上留下记号。

pos.zh: 名词：品牌；商标；种类；烙印
动词：打烙印；给……定性；给……加上污名

senses.title: A product name or mark
senses.definition: a name, sign or design that a company puts on its goods to show they are its own
senses.definitionCN: 公司印在商品上、表明商品归属的名称、标志或图案
senses.example: This shoe brand is popular with young runners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个运动鞋品牌很受年轻跑者欢迎。
senses.why: A burned mark once proved who owned a thing, and a printed name now proves which company made it.
senses.whyCN: 烧出的记号曾用来证明东西归谁所有，如今印上的名称则证明商品出自哪家公司。

senses.title: A particular type
senses.definition: a particular kind of something, especially one with a special quality
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的特定种类，尤指带有某种独特性质的种类
senses.example: He has a strange brand of humour.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一种古怪的幽默。
senses.why: A mark separated one owner's cattle from another's, so the word came to separate one kind of thing from another.
senses.whyCN: 记号曾把一户人家的牛与别人家的牛分开，于是这个词又用来把一种事物与另一种区分开。

senses.title: A burned mark
senses.definition: a mark burned onto the skin of an animal or a person with a hot iron
senses.definitionCN: 用烧红的铁器烙在动物或人皮肤上的记号
senses.example: The old horse still carried the brand of its first owner.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹老马身上仍带着第一位主人的烙印。
senses.why: Old English brand meant a burning piece of wood, and the mark that such a stick left took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 brand 指一块燃烧的木头，这种木条留下的记号便沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: To mark or label
senses.definition: to burn a mark on something, or to describe someone in a way that is hard to escape
senses.definitionCN: 在物体上烙下记号，或以难以摆脱的方式给某人贴上标签
senses.example: The papers branded him a troublemaker.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把他定性为惹事的人。
senses.why: A hot iron left a mark that could not be washed off, and a fixed label works on a person in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 烧红的铁器留下的记号洗不掉，而一个固定的标签加在人身上，作用完全一样。

intro.en: Brand began as a word for fire, then for the mark fire leaves, and only later for a company's name.
intro.cn: brand 最初指火，继而指火留下的记号，最后才指公司的名称。

items.en: Brand first meant a flame or a burning piece of wood.
items.cn: brand 最初指火焰或一块燃烧的木头。

items.en: Close words in Dutch and German still carry the sense of burning.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语中的近亲词仍带着「燃烧」的意思。

items.en: A hot iron left a brand on animals and barrels to show who owned them.
items.cn: 烧红的铁器在牲畜与木桶上留下烙印，用以表明归属。

items.en: In the nineteenth century makers printed a mark on goods, and called it a brand.
items.cn: 十九世纪，制造者在商品上印上标记，并称之为 brand。

items.en: Today the brand is the name of a product, and the verb can label a person for good.
items.cn: 今天 brand 指商品的名称，动词则可给人定下难以摆脱的标签。

root: brand 在古英语中意为火焰或一块燃烧的木头，与荷兰语、德语中的近亲词同源。烧红的铁器在牲畜与木桶上烙下记号，用来表明归属，这个词便转而指记号本身。十九世纪，制造者把标记印在商品上并称之为 brand，于是它又获得了「品牌」的现代意义。今天 brand 既是商品名称，也可作动词给人定下标签。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of brand stand on one picture: a hot iron leaving a mark that cannot be washed away.
sensesIntro.cn: brand 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：烧红的铁器留下一个洗不掉的记号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hot iron pressing a mark onto wood or hide
core.cn: 核心意象：烧红的铁器在木头或兽皮上压出记号

branches.en: THE NAME: a printed mark now tells which company made the goods.
branches.cn: 名称线：印上的标记如今说明商品出自哪家公司。

branches.en: THE TYPE: a mark also sets one kind apart from another.
branches.cn: 种类线：记号也把一种事物与另一种区分开。

branches.en: THE SCAR: the burned mark on hide is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 烙印线：烙在兽皮上的记号是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the verb marks a thing or pins a name on a person.
branches.cn: 贴标线：动词既给物烙记号，也给人定标签。

branches.en: THE IRON: the mark and the act of burning share one tool.
branches.cn: 烙铁线：记号与烙的动作共用同一件工具。

intro.en: Brand is a base noun and verb, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: brand 是基础名词兼动词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nota and titulus mean a mark and a label; they are parallels, not the source of brand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nota 与 titulus 分别意为「记号」与「标签」，它们是平行词，不是 brand 的来源。

items.example: The oldest sense is a flame.

items.meaning: the word by which a thing is known
the picture people have of something

definition_zh: 勇敢的；无所畏惧的；需要勇气的；勇敢面对（危险）；壮丽的（书面）
definition_en: ready to face danger, pain or difficulty without fear, and to go out and meet such danger, or (in old use) fine and splendid
core_image: 大风里仍向前迈步、不肯后退的人
scene: 悬崖边，少年顶着风把被困的小狗抱了回来。The brave boy carried the trapped dog back from the cliff.
sceneCN: 这里 brave 是「勇敢的」（第 1 个义项：面对危险不退缩）；句意为那个勇敢的男孩把被困的小狗从悬崖边抱了回来。

pos.zh: 形容词：勇敢的；无所畏惧的；壮丽的
动词：勇敢面对；冒着（危险、恶劣天气）

derivatives.zh: 由 brave 加 -ery 构成，义为「勇敢；勇气」
由 brave 加 -ly 构成，义为「勇敢地」
与 brave 同源，义为「逞强；虚张声势的勇气」

senses.title: Ready to face danger
senses.definition: ready to face danger, pain or difficulty without fear
senses.definitionCN: 面对危险、痛苦或困难而不畏惧
senses.example: The brave girl saved the cat from the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那个勇敢的女孩把猫从河里救了出来。
senses.why: Italian bravo first described a bold, wild person, and that boldness became the heart of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 bravo 最初形容大胆、不驯的人，这种胆气后来成了这个词义的核心。

senses.title: To face danger or bad weather
senses.definition: to face danger, bad weather or difficulty in order to do something
senses.definitionCN: 为了做某事而直面危险、恶劣天气或困难
senses.example: The fishermen braved the storm to reach the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 渔民们冒着风暴驶向港口。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb: instead of running from the danger, a person goes out and meets it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了动词：人不是躲开危险，而是主动走出去迎上去。

senses.title: Fine and splendid
senses.definition: fine, splendid or showy, now mostly kept in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 美好的、壮丽的或引人注目的，今多保留在固定短语中
senses.example: They set out for a brave new world.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出发前往一个美丽的新世界。
senses.why: In older use brave meant showy and splendid, and this sense survives in a few set phrases.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法里 brave 意为华丽、壮美，这个义项只保留在少数固定短语中。

intro.en: Brave came through French and Italian from a word for wild and bold, and it has softened into praise.
intro.cn: brave 经由法语和意大利语来自一个意为「野性、大胆」的词，后来变成了赞美之词。

items.en: The trail starts at barbarus, a word for a foreigner seen as wild.
items.cn: 这条线索始于 barbarus，指被视为野性的外邦人。

items.en: Italian bravo meant bold, wild or ready to fight.
items.cn: 意大利语 bravo 意为大胆、不驯或随时准备动手。

items.en: French took the word and used it for a fine, showy and daring person.
items.cn: 法语借入这个词，用来形容出色、气派又胆大的人。

items.en: English borrowed it and made courage the main sense.
items.cn: 英语借入后，把「勇气」发展成了主要义项。

items.en: Today brave praises courage, and the verb means to face danger on purpose.
items.cn: 今天 brave 用来称赞勇气，动词则指有意直面危险。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about courage.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与勇气有关的词。

entries.definition: A part that slows or stops a vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「刹车」，读音与 brave 接近。

entries.definition: A place where a dead person is buried.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坟墓」，拼写与 brave 相近。

entries.definition: To want something very strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「渴望」，拼写与 brave 相近。

entries.definition: Willing to take risks without fear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大胆的」，指敢于冒险而不畏惧。

entries.definition: Showing no fear at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无畏的」。

entries.definition: Brave in a way that people admire.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有勇气的；英勇的」。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Italian bravo meant bold and wild, and English kept the boldness as courage.
normal.cn: 意大利语 bravo 意为大胆不驯，英语把这份胆气留作「勇气」。

normal.en: The adjective became a verb, so to brave the storm is to walk into it.
normal.cn: 形容词变成了动词，所以 brave the storm 就是迎着风暴走进去。

normal.en: An older sense meant splendid, and it survives in a brave new world.
normal.cn: 较早的义项意为壮丽，它保存在 a brave new world 这个短语里。

normal.en: It often pairs with face, storm and cold.
normal.cn: 它常与 face、storm、cold 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-a-v-e; the silent e keeps the long vowel.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-a-v-e，词尾不发音的 e 让元音读长音。

abstract.en: See a small figure leaning into a strong wind, still moving forward: that is brave.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小小的人影顶着强风，仍一步步向前：这就是 brave。

abstract.en: The same figure can stand for a storm walker or for someone facing bad news.
abstract.cn: 同一个人影既可以指迎着风暴走路的人，也可以指面对坏消息的人。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the wind bring the courage back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那阵风把勇气带回来。

examples.en: The brave girl saved the cat from the river.
examples.cn: 那个勇敢的女孩把猫从河里救了出来。

examples.en: The fishermen braved the storm to reach the harbour.
examples.cn: 渔民们冒着风暴驶向港口。

examples.en: They set out for a brave new world.
examples.cn: 他们出发前往一个美丽的新世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不累夫」——顶着大风也不后退的人：勇敢的

root: brave 经由法语与意大利语上溯到拉丁语 barbarus，原指被视为野性的外邦人。意大利语 bravo 意为大胆不驯，法语用来形容出色而胆大的人，英语借入后把「勇气」发展为主要义项。今天 brave 用来称赞面对危险不退缩的人，也可作动词表示主动迎向危险；另有一个较旧的义项意为壮丽，只保留在少数固定短语中。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of brave rest on one picture: a person who moves toward danger instead of away from it.
sensesIntro.cn: brave 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个人朝危险走过去，而不是躲开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure leaning into the wind and still moving forward
core.cn: 核心意象：顶着风仍向前迈步的人

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one who is ready to face danger is the first sense.
branches.cn: 人物线：面对危险不退缩的人是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE DEED: the verb is the act of walking into the danger.
branches.cn: 行动线：动词指走进危险里的那个动作。

branches.en: THE SPLENDOUR: the old sense of something fine and showy.
branches.cn: 壮丽线：那个意为出色、气派的旧义项。

branches.en: THE COURAGE: the person and the deed share one fearless spirit.
branches.cn: 勇气线：人与行动共享同一种无所畏惧的精神。

branches.en: THE SHOW: braving a danger and a splendid display both put a person on view.
branches.cn: 显露线：直面危险与华丽场面都把一个人显现在众人眼前。

items.meaning: a calm look shown to others
very bad weather with strong wind

definition_zh: 面包；生计；钱（俚语）
definition_en: a food made from flour and water and baked in an oven, the money or food a person needs to live, or (in slang) money
core_image: 刚从炉子里取出、外皮焦黄的一整条面食
scene: 清晨的厨房里，刚出炉的面包冒着热气，她把它切成片抹上黄油。Warm bread came out of the oven and she cut it into slices.
sceneCN: 这里 bread 是「面包」（第 1 个义项：用面粉与水烘烤成的食物）；句意为温热的面包刚出炉，她把它切片抹上黄油。

pos.zh: 名词：面包；生计；钱
动词：给……裹上面包屑

collocations.zh: 面包与黄油；主要收入来源

derivatives.zh: 与 bread 同源，义为「宽度；广度」，源自古英语表示「宽」的词
由 bread 加 -ed 构成，义为「裹了面包屑的」
由 bread 与 basket 组合而成，义为「面包篮；产粮区」

senses.title: The baked food
senses.definition: a food made from flour, water and usually yeast, baked in an oven
senses.definitionCN: 用面粉、水，通常还加酵母，在炉中烤成的食物
senses.example: She bought a loaf of bread on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在回家路上买了一条面包。
senses.why: Old English bread meant a piece or crumb, and that word slowly took the place of the older name for the baked loaf.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bread 意为「一块、碎屑」，这个词慢慢取代了原来指烤制面包的旧名称。

senses.title: Food and money to live
senses.definition: the money or food that a person needs in order to live
senses.definitionCN: 一个人维持生活所需的钱或食物
senses.example: He earns his bread as a taxi driver.
senses.exampleCN: 他开出租车挣饭吃。
senses.why: Bread was the basic food of daily life, so the word stood for the whole means of living.
senses.whyCN: 面包曾是日常饮食的基础，于是这个词被用来指整套谋生的手段。

senses.title: Money
senses.definition: money, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用手指钱
senses.example: They started the band just to make some bread.
senses.exampleCN: 他们组乐队就是为了挣点钱。
senses.why: Because bread kept people alive, street slang used the word for the money that buys it.
senses.whyCN: 因为面包养活了人，街头俚语便用这个词指买面包的钱。

intro.en: Bread first meant a crumb or a piece, then the whole loaf, and later the living it stands for.
intro.cn: bread 最初指碎屑或一小块，后来指整条面包，再引申为它所代表的生计。

items.en: Bread meant a piece, a crumb or a morsel of food.
items.cn: bread 意为一块、碎屑或一小口食物。

items.cn: 这个词与一个意为「酿造」的古动词相连，与 brew 同出一族。

items.en: Bread replaced the older word for the baked loaf and became the everyday name for it.
items.cn: bread 取代了原来指烤制面包的旧词，成为它的日常名称。

items.en: As the main food of the table, bread came to mean the means of living.
items.cn: 面包是餐桌上的主食，于是又引申为谋生的手段。

items.en: In modern street slang bread also means money, the thing that buys the loaf.
items.cn: 在现代街头俚语中，bread 还指钱，也就是买面包的东西。

root: bread 在古英语中意为一块、碎屑，与一个表示「酿造」的古动词相连，和 brew 同出一族。它后来取代了原来指烤制面包的旧词，成为这种主食的日常名称；因为面包是餐桌上的主食，这个词又引申为谋生的手段，现代街头俚语里还用来指钱。今天 bread 主要指面包，也可指生计与钞票。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of bread grow from one picture: a warm loaf that keeps a person alive.
sensesIntro.cn: bread 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一条让人活下去的热面包。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm loaf fresh from the oven
core.cn: 核心意象：刚从炉子里取出的热面包

branches.en: THE LOAF: the baked food itself is the first sense.
branches.cn: 面包线：烤好的食物本身是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE LIVING: the staple food stands for the means of life.
branches.cn: 生计线：主食代指维持生活的手段。

branches.en: THE CASH: slang uses the loaf for the money that buys it.
branches.cn: 钞票线：俚语用面包指买它的钱。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the loaf and the living both centre on the daily meal.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：面包与生计都围绕每日的一餐。

branches.en: THE PRICE: earning a living and making money are two sides of one need.
branches.cn: 价钱线：挣饭吃与挣钱是同一需求的两面。

definition_zh: 打破；碎裂；弄坏；违犯；打断；散开；休息；机会
definition_en: to separate into pieces, damage something, disobey a rule, interrupt something, or end a group, and the pause or chance that comes from such a split
core_image: 一整块东西受力后从中间裂开
scene: 厨房里，孩子松手，玻璃杯掉在地板上摔成了几片。The glass fell and broke on the kitchen floor.
sceneCN: 这里 break 是「打破；碎裂」（第 1 个义项：受外力而分成几块）；句意为玻璃杯掉在厨房地板上摔碎了。

pos.zh: 动词：打破；损坏；违犯；打断；散开
名词：休息；课间；机会；裂口

derivatives.zh: 由 break 加 -able 构成，义为「易碎的；会破的」
由 break 加 -age 构成，义为「破损；破损物」
由 break 加 -er 构成，义为「破坏者；碎浪」
由 breakable 加 un- 构成，义为「牢不可破的」
由 out 与 break 组合而成，义为「爆发；突然发生」

senses.title: To split into pieces
senses.definition: to separate into pieces as a result of a blow or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 因撞击或压力而分成若干块
senses.example: The glass fell and broke on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃杯掉在地上摔碎了。
senses.why: Old English brecan meant to separate something by force, and the picture of pieces falling apart is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 brecan 意为用力把东西分开，碎片散落的画面正是最古老的义项。

senses.title: To damage a machine
senses.definition: to damage something so that it no longer works
senses.definitionCN: 损坏某物，使它无法正常工作
senses.example: He broke his watch by dropping it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把手表摔坏了。
senses.why: A machine is a whole made of connected parts; once the parts split, the whole can no longer work.
senses.whyCN: 机器是由相连部件构成的整体；部件一旦裂开，整体就无法运转。

senses.title: To disobey a rule
senses.definition: to fail to keep a rule, a law or a promise
senses.definitionCN: 未能遵守规则、法律或诺言
senses.example: You break the rule if you ride without a helmet.
senses.exampleCN: 不戴头盔骑车就违犯了规定。
senses.why: A rule or a promise is pictured as a solid thing, and disobeying it snaps that thing apart.
senses.whyCN: 规则或许诺被想象成一件结实的东西，违背它就是把这件东西折断。

senses.title: To interrupt
senses.definition: to interrupt something or bring it to a sudden pause
senses.definitionCN: 打断某事，使之突然停顿
senses.example: She broke the silence with a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一句笑话打破了沉默。
senses.why: Silence and talk flow like a line, and a sudden sound cuts that line in two.
senses.whyCN: 沉默与谈话像一条线一样延续，突然的声音把这条线切成两段。

senses.title: A short rest
senses.definition: a short period of rest between parts of work or study
senses.definitionCN: 工作或学习之间短暂的休息时间
senses.example: We have a short break between classes.
senses.exampleCN: 我们课间有一小段休息。
senses.why: A pause splits the day into two parts, just as a break splits a solid object into two.
senses.whyCN: 暂停把一天分成两段，正如 break 把一件实心的东西分成两块。

senses.title: A chance to succeed
senses.definition: a chance, especially one that helps someone succeed
senses.definitionCN: 机会，尤指帮助某人取得成功的机会
senses.example: Give the young actor a break.
senses.exampleCN: 给这个年轻演员一次机会吧。
senses.why: When a hard situation opens, its barrier breaks, and the open path is a chance to move forward.
senses.whyCN: 困难的局面一旦打开，挡在前面的屏障就破了，敞开的通道就是向前的机会。

senses.title: To end a group or a bond
senses.definition: to end a relationship or a group so that its members separate
senses.definitionCN: 结束一段关系或一个团体，使成员各自分开
senses.example: The band broke up last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐队去年解散了。
senses.why: A group is held together like one solid object; when the bond snaps, the members scatter.
senses.whyCN: 团体像一整块东西那样连在一起；纽带一断，成员就四散而去。

intro.en: Break goes back to an old root for splitting, and its senses have spread from objects to rules, days and chances.
intro.cn: break 可上溯到一个表示「裂开」的古老词根，词义从物体扩展到规则、日子与机会。

items.en: A deep root with the sense of breaking or bursting stands behind the word.
items.cn: 这个词背后有一个表示「破裂、爆开」的古老词根。

items.en: Brecan meant to break or fracture something by force.
items.cn: brecan 意为用力打破或折断某物。

items.en: Dutch breken and German brechen still carry the same meaning.
items.cn: 荷兰语 breken 与德语 brechen 仍保持同样的意思。

items.en: The verb passed into Middle English as break and kept the sense of splitting.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中古英语时写作 break，保留了「裂开」的意思。

items.en: A gap, a pause or a piece of broken time came to be called a break.
items.cn: 空隙、暂停或被打断的一段时间也开始被称作 break。

items.en: Today break covers splitting, damage, rules, pauses and the chance that follows a split.
items.cn: 今天 break 覆盖破碎、损坏、违规、暂停，以及裂缝之后出现的机会。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about cracking and pausing.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与破裂、暂停有关的词。

entries.definition: A part that slows or stops a vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「刹车」，读音与 break 相同。

entries.definition: Cold, empty and without hope.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒凉的；凄冷的」，拼写与 break 相近。

entries.definition: A hard block used for building walls.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「砖」，拼写与 break 相近。

entries.definition: To make a line of damage without falling apart.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「裂开；出现裂缝」，但未必碎成块。

entries.definition: To hit something so hard that it breaks loudly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「猛砸；砸碎」。

entries.definition: To break suddenly into many small pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「粉碎」，指突然碎成许多小块。

entries.definition: A short stop before continuing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暂停」，指继续之前的短暂停顿。

entries.definition: An opening that may lead to success.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机会」，指可能带来成功的时机。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English brecan meant to break by force, and that picture of splitting is still sense one.
normal.cn: 古英语 brecan 意为用力打破，那个裂开的画面至今仍是第一个义项。

normal.en: A rule is pictured as a solid thing, so disobeying it is breaking it.
normal.cn: 规则被想象成一件结实的东西，所以不遵守就是把它折断。

normal.en: A pause splits the day in two, which is why a rest is called a break.
normal.cn: 暂停把一天切成两段，所以休息也被称作 break。

normal.en: It often pairs with ice, record, promise and down.
normal.cn: 它常与 ice、record、promise、down 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-e-a-k; the past tense is broke and the participle is broken.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-e-a-k；过去式是 broke，过去分词是 broken。

abstract.en: See a whole plate hit the floor and split into bright pieces: that is break.
abstract.cn: 想象一整只盘子落地，裂成几块亮闪闪的碎片：这就是 break。

abstract.en: Let a pause cut the same line in two and the plate becomes a rest.
abstract.cn: 让一个停顿把同一条线切成两段，那只盘子就变成了「休息」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the cracked plate bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那只裂开的盘子把意思带回来。

examples.en: The glass fell and broke on the floor.
examples.cn: 玻璃杯掉在地上摔碎了。

examples.en: We have a short break between classes.
examples.cn: 我们课间有一小段休息。

examples.en: The band broke up last year.
examples.cn: 这个乐队去年解散了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不累克」——整块东西一受力就裂开：打破

root: break 可上溯到一个表示「破裂」的古老词根，古英语写作 brecan，意为用力打破或折断，与荷兰语 breken、德语 brechen 同源。词义从物体碎裂扩展到机器损坏、违背规则、打断话语与团体解散；空隙与暂停也被称作 break，而裂缝打开后出现的通路又引申为「机会」。

sensesIntro.en: All seven senses of break grow from one picture: a solid whole splitting apart under force.
sensesIntro.cn: break 的七个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一整块实心的东西在受力后裂开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid whole splitting apart under force
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块实心的东西在受力后裂开

branches.en: THE PIECES: the literal splitting of an object is the first sense.
branches.cn: 碎片线：物体被分成几块的字面义是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a broken whole can no longer do its work.
branches.cn: 机器线：整体破了，就无法再运转。

branches.en: THE RULE: a promise or law is snapped like a solid stick.
branches.cn: 规则线：诺言或法律像一根实心木棍那样被折断。

branches.en: THE CUT: a sudden sound cuts a flow of talk in two.
branches.cn: 切断线：突然的声音把一段话语切成两半。

branches.en: THE GAP: a pause and an opening are both gaps left by a split.
branches.cn: 空隙线：暂停与机会都是裂开后留下的空隙。

intro.en: Break is a base verb and noun, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: break 是基础动词兼名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere means to break, and ruptura means a break; they are parallels, not the source of break.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frangere 意为「打破」，ruptura 意为「裂口」，它们是平行词，不是 break 的来源。

items.example: Brecan is the recorded Old English source.
items.exampleCN: brecan 是有记录的古英语来源。

definition_zh: 早餐；早饭；早餐时分；吃早餐
definition_en: the first meal of the day, the occasion of eating it, or to eat this first meal
core_image: 清晨桌上摆好的一杯热奶与几片面包
scene: 清晨的餐桌上摆着热牛奶、鸡蛋和切片面包，一家人围坐在一起。Breakfast was ready on the table with hot milk, eggs and sliced bread.
sceneCN: 这里 breakfast 是「早餐」（第 1 个义项：一天中的第一顿饭）；句意为餐桌上摆好了热牛奶、鸡蛋和切片面包。

pos.zh: 名词：早餐；早饭；早餐时分
动词：吃早餐

derivatives.zh: 由 breakfast 加 -less 构成，义为「没吃早餐的」
由 breakfast 加 -ing 构成，义为「吃早餐这件事」
由 bed、and 与 breakfast 组合而成，义为「提供住宿与早餐的小旅馆」

senses.title: The first meal of the day
senses.definition: the first meal of the day, eaten in the morning
senses.definitionCN: 一天中的第一顿饭，在早晨吃
senses.example: I had eggs and toast for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 我早餐吃了鸡蛋和吐司。
senses.why: The word is built from break and fast: the morning meal breaks the long fast of the night.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 break 与 fast 组成：早餐打破了整夜不进食的斋戒。

senses.title: The occasion of the first meal
senses.definition: the time or occasion when this first meal is eaten, often with over or at
senses.definitionCN: 吃这顿早饭的时间或场合，常与 over、at 连用
senses.example: We talked about the trip over breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃早餐时聊了这次旅行。
senses.why: Because the meal marks a fixed point in the morning, the word also names the time around it.
senses.whyCN: 因为这顿饭标出了早晨的一个固定时段，这个词也用来指那段时间。

senses.title: To eat the first meal
senses.definition: to eat breakfast
senses.definitionCN: 吃早餐
senses.example: They breakfasted early and left at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 他们早早吃了早餐，七点就出发了。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the act of taking that first meal.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，用来指吃这第一顿饭的动作。

intro.en: Breakfast is a compound that replaced an older name for the morning meal by describing what that meal does.
intro.cn: breakfast 是一个复合词，它用描述这顿饭作用的方式，取代了早餐的旧名称。

items.en: The first meal was once called morning meat, the food of the morning.
items.cn: 第一顿饭曾被称为 morning meat，即早晨的食物。

items.en: The new name joined break with fast, the long night without food.
items.cn: 新名称把 break 与 fast 结合，后者指整夜不进食的斋戒。

items.en: Breakfast took the place of the old name and became the everyday word.
items.cn: breakfast 取代了旧名称，成为日常用词。

items.en: People who began work at dawn needed a quick meal, and the word spread with that habit.
items.cn: 天亮就上工的人需要一顿快餐，这个词随这一习惯传播开来。

items.en: Today breakfast is the standard name for the first meal, and a verb means to eat it.
items.cn: 今天 breakfast 是第一顿饭的标准名称，动词则指吃这顿饭。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects the other meals of the day.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收一天中其他几顿饭的名称。

entries.definition: To split, the first part of this compound word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打破」，是这个复合词的前半部分。

entries.definition: A period of not eating, the second part of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斋戒」，是这个复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: An informal British word for breakfast.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式口语中指「早餐」，读音与 breakfast 接近。

entries.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「午餐」。

entries.definition: The main meal of the day, usually in the evening.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「晚餐；正餐」。

entries.definition: A late morning meal that replaces breakfast and lunch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「早午餐」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Breakfast is break plus fast: the meal breaks the night's long fast.
normal.cn: breakfast 是 break 加 fast：这顿饭打破了整夜的斋戒。

normal.en: It replaced the older name morning meat in Middle English.
normal.cn: 它在中古英语时期取代了旧名称 morning meat。

normal.en: People who started work at dawn made a quick meal a daily habit.
normal.cn: 天亮上工的人把一顿快餐变成了每日习惯。

normal.en: It often pairs with have, time, quick and skip.
normal.cn: 它常与 have、time、quick、skip 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-e-a-k-f-a-s-t; the two old words are still visible inside it.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-e-a-k-f-a-s-t，两个旧词仍清晰可见。

abstract.en: See a warm cup and a plate of bread waiting on a morning table: that is breakfast.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨的桌上摆着一杯热饮和一盘面包：这就是 breakfast。

abstract.en: Add a clock at seven and the same table becomes the time of breakfast.
abstract.cn: 在桌旁加一只指着七点的钟，同一幅画面就变成「早餐时分」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the morning table bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那张清晨的餐桌把意思带回来。

examples.en: I had eggs and toast for breakfast.
examples.cn: 我早餐吃了鸡蛋和吐司。

examples.en: We talked about the trip over breakfast.
examples.cn: 我们吃早餐时聊了这次旅行。

examples.en: They breakfasted early and left at seven.
examples.cn: 他们早早吃了早餐，七点就出发了。

root: breakfast 是一个复合词，由 break（打破）与 fast（斋戒）组成，字面意思就是「打破斋戒」。古英语中原先用 morning meat 指早晨的食物，中古英语时期 breakfast 取代了旧名称。天亮上工的人需要一顿快餐，这个词随这一习惯传播开来。今天它指一天中的第一顿饭，也可指吃早餐的时间，还能作动词表示「吃早餐」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of breakfast rest on one picture: the morning table that ends the night without food.
sensesIntro.cn: breakfast 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：那张结束整夜空腹的清晨餐桌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a morning table with a warm drink and bread
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨摆着热饮与面包的餐桌

branches.en: THE MEAL: the food itself is the first sense.
branches.cn: 饭食线：这顿饭的食物本身是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE HOUR: the meal also names the time around it.
branches.cn: 时段线：这顿饭也用来指它前后那段时间。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the eating of the first meal.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指吃这第一顿饭的动作。

branches.en: THE TABLE: food and the hour both gather around the morning table.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：食物与时段都围绕清晨的餐桌。

branches.en: THE ROUTINE: a fixed hour and a repeated act become a daily habit.
branches.cn: 习惯线：固定的时段与重复的动作合成每日习惯。

intro.en: Breakfast is a compound of two old words, so the items below are its halves and its endings.
intro.cn: breakfast 由两个古老词组合而成，下面列出的是它的两半与词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ientaculum means a morning meal; it is a parallel term, not the source of breakfast.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ientaculum 意为「早餐」，它是平行词，不是 breakfast 的来源。

items.example: It is the first half of breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 它是 breakfast 的前半部分。

items.example: It is the second half of breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 它是 breakfast 的后半部分。

items.meaning: a piece of furniture for eating

definition_zh: 呼吸；一口气；口气、呼出的气；一丝微风；顺畅呼吸的状态
definition_en: an amount of air taken into the lungs, the air that comes out of the mouth, a very slight movement of air, or the state of breathing easily
core_image: 口鼻前呼出的一团淡淡白气
scene: 跑完步，他站在跑道边弯下腰，想喘匀这口气。After the race he stood by the track, trying to catch his breath.
sceneCN: 这里 breath 是「呼吸；一口气」（第 1 个义项：吸入又呼出的一股空气）；句意为跑完步后他站在跑道边，想把这口气喘匀。

pos.zh: 名词：呼吸；一口气；口气；一丝微风

derivatives.zh: 与 breath 同源，义为「呼吸」
由 breathe 加 -ing 构成，义为「呼吸；呼吸动作」
由 breath 加 -less 构成，义为「喘不上气的；屏息的」
由 breath 与 taking 组合而成，义为「令人惊叹的；惊险的」

senses.title: One amount of air taken in
senses.definition: an amount of air taken into the lungs and then let out
senses.definitionCN: 吸入肺里再呼出的一股空气
senses.example: He took a deep breath before he jumped.
senses.exampleCN: 他跳之前深吸了一口气。
senses.why: Old English braeth first meant vapour or smell, the mist that leaves the mouth, and the air taken in took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 braeth 最初指蒸气或气味，也就是离开嘴边的雾气，吸入的空气也沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: The air that comes out
senses.definition: the air that comes out of your mouth, especially when it has a smell
senses.definitionCN: 从嘴里呼出的气，尤指带气味时
senses.example: Onions can give you bad breath.
senses.exampleCN: 吃洋葱会让人有口臭。
senses.why: What leaves the body as vapour became the everyday word for the smell of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 以蒸气形式离开身体的东西，后来成了日常指口腔气味的词。

senses.title: A slight movement of air
senses.definition: a very small amount of wind or moving air
senses.definitionCN: 极少量流动的空气或风
senses.example: Not a breath of wind moved the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 一丝风也没有，树叶纹丝不动。
senses.why: A small puff of air looks like a single breath, so the word named the faintest wind.
senses.whyCN: 一小股空气看起来就像呼出的一口气，于是这个词也用来指最轻微的风。

senses.title: The state of breathing easily
senses.definition: the state of being able to breathe easily, chiefly in phrases such as out of breath
senses.definitionCN: 能够轻松呼吸的状态，主要用于 out of breath 这类短语
senses.example: The long climb left him out of breath.
senses.exampleCN: 那段长长的攀爬让他上气不接下气。
senses.why: The word for the air also names the easy flow of that air; when the flow stops, a person is out of breath.
senses.whyCN: 指空气的词也用来指空气顺畅的流动；流动一断，人就上气不接下气。

intro.en: Breath began as a word for vapour and smell, then narrowed to the air a person breathes.
intro.cn: breath 最初指蒸气与气味，后来缩小为一个人呼吸的空气。

items.en: Braeth meant vapour, smell or the mist of the mouth.
items.cn: braeth 意为蒸气、气味或口中的雾气。

items.en: German Brodem and Dutch braam carry a nearby sense of steam or smell.
items.cn: 德语 Brodem 与荷兰语 braam 都带有蒸气或气味的意思。

items.en: The word narrowed to the air a living body takes in and sends out.
items.cn: 这个词缩小为活着的身体吸入与呼出的空气。

items.en: Breath kept this sense, while the verb breathe grew beside it.
items.cn: breath 保留了这一义项，动词 breathe 在它旁边发展出来。

items.en: Today breath also names a faint wind and the easy flow of air in the body.
items.cn: 今天 breath 还指微弱的风，以及体内空气的顺畅流动。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about air and breathing.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与空气、呼吸有关的词。

entries.definition: The verb that means to take air in and out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「呼吸」，与 breath 同源。

entries.definition: A gap made in a wall or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺口；违反」，读音与 breath 接近。

entries.definition: Air moving across the land.

normal.en: Old English braeth meant vapour, and the mist of the mouth is still the picture behind it.
normal.cn: 古英语 braeth 意为蒸气，口中的雾气至今仍是它背后的画面。

normal.en: The word then narrowed to the air a body takes in and sends out.
normal.cn: 这个词随后缩小为身体吸入与呼出的空气。

normal.en: A tiny puff of air looks like one breath, so a faint wind is a breath of wind.
normal.cn: 一小股空气就像一口气，所以微弱的风叫作 a breath of wind。

normal.en: It often pairs with deep, out of, bad and hold.
normal.cn: 它常与 deep、out of、bad、hold 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-e-a-t-h; it is the noun, while breathe is the verb.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-e-a-t-h，它是名词，动词则是 breathe。

abstract.en: See a faint white cloud leave a mouth on a cold morning: that cloud is breath.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷的清晨，嘴边飘出一小团白气：那团白气就是 breath。

abstract.en: Thin that cloud until it barely moves a leaf and it becomes a breath of wind.
abstract.cn: 把这团白气稀释到几乎吹不动一片叶子，它就变成了「一丝微风」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the white cloud bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那团白气把意思带回来。

examples.en: He took a deep breath before he jumped.
examples.cn: 他跳之前深吸了一口气。

examples.en: Onions can give you bad breath.
examples.cn: 吃洋葱会让人有口臭。

examples.en: The long climb left him out of breath.
examples.cn: 那段长长的攀爬让他上气不接下气。

root: breath 在古英语中写作 braeth，意为蒸气、气味或口中的雾气，与德语 Brodem、荷兰语 braam 有相近的含义。后来词义缩小为活着的身体吸入与呼出的空气，动词 breathe 也在它旁边发展出来。今天 breath 指一次呼吸、呼出的口气、一丝微风，以及顺畅呼吸的状态。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of breath grow from one picture: a faint cloud of air leaving the mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: breath 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：从嘴边飘出的一小团淡淡白气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faint cloud of air in front of the mouth
core.cn: 核心意象：口鼻前呼出的一小团淡淡白气

branches.en: THE INTAKE: one amount of air taken in and let out.
branches.cn: 吸气线：吸入又呼出的一股空气。

branches.en: THE EXHALE: the air leaving the mouth and its smell.
branches.cn: 呼气线：离开嘴边的空气及它的气味。

branches.en: THE BREEZE: a puff of air too small to be called wind.
branches.cn: 微风线：小到称不上风的一股空气。

branches.en: THE FLOW: breathing easily or losing that ease.
branches.cn: 流动线：呼吸顺畅，或失去这份顺畅。

branches.en: THE CLOUD: air going in and air coming out share one visible mist.
branches.cn: 白气线：吸入与呼出的空气共享同一团可见的雾气。

items.exampleCN: braeth 是有记录的古英语形式。

definition_zh: 呼吸；呼出；低声说；注入（活力）
definition_en: to take air into the lungs and let it out, to send air or words out softly, or to fill something with life or a quality
core_image: 胸腔一起一伏，把空气吸进来再送出去
scene: 潜水员浮出水面，摘下呼吸管，深深地吸了一口空气。The diver surfaced, took off the tube and began to breathe deeply.
sceneCN: 这里 breathe 是「呼吸」（第 1 个义项：把空气吸入肺里再呼出）；句意为潜水员浮出水面，摘下管子，开始深呼吸。

pos.zh: 动词：呼吸；呼出；低声说；注入

derivatives.zh: 与 breathe 同源，义为「呼吸；一口气」
由 breathe 加 -ing 构成，义为「呼吸；呼吸动作」
由 breathe 加 -able 构成，义为「可以呼吸的；透气的」
由 breathe 加 -er 构成，义为「短暂的休息；喘口气」

senses.title: To take air in and out
senses.definition: to take air into the lungs and let it out again
senses.definitionCN: 把空气吸入肺里再呼出来
senses.example: Fish cannot breathe out of water.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼离开水就无法呼吸。
senses.why: The verb grew beside the noun breath, naming the act of moving air in and out of the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在名词 breath 旁边发展出来，用来指把空气送进身体再送出去的动作。

senses.title: To send out air or soft words
senses.definition: to send air out of the body, or to say something in a soft voice
senses.definitionCN: 把空气送出体外，或以轻柔的声音说话
senses.example: She breathed a quiet warning in his ear.
senses.exampleCN: 她在他耳边低声警告了一句。
senses.why: The air that leaves the mouth can carry a whisper, so the same act came to mean speaking softly.
senses.whyCN: 离开嘴边的空气可以承载耳语，于是同一个动作又用来指轻声说话。

senses.title: To fill with life or a quality
senses.definition: to give life, energy or a particular quality to something
senses.definitionCN: 给某物注入生命、活力或某种特质
senses.example: The new players breathed life into the team.
senses.exampleCN: 新队员给球队注入了活力。
senses.why: Breath is the visible sign of life, so pouring breath into a thing means waking it up.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸是生命可见的标志，所以把气息灌进某物，就意味着让它活起来。

intro.en: Breathe is the old verb formed from breath, and it has kept the sense of moving air ever since.
intro.cn: breathe 是由 breath 构成的古老动词，一直保留着「让空气流动」的意思。

items.en: Braethian was the verb built on braeth, meaning to send out vapour or air.
items.cn: braethian 是建立在 braeth 之上的动词，意为呼出蒸气或空气。

items.en: German brodeln and Dutch braemen keep the sense of steaming or breathing out.
items.cn: 德语 brodeln 与荷兰语 braemen 保留了「冒气、呼出」的意思。

items.en: The verb settled as breathe and took the full sense of taking air in and out.
items.cn: 这个动词固定为 breathe，并获得了「吸入与呼出空气」的完整含义。

items.en: Because a whisper rides on the breath, the verb also came to mean to say something softly.
items.cn: 因为耳语随气息而出，这个动词也引申为轻声说话。

items.en: Today breathe covers breathing, whispering and giving life to something.
items.cn: 今天 breathe 覆盖呼吸、低声细语，以及给某物注入生命。

sensesIntro.cn: breathe 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：空气进出身体。

core.cn: 核心意象：胸腔一起一伏，空气进出

branches.en: THE AIR: moving air in and out is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 空气线：空气进出是第一个也是最字面的义项。

branches.en: THE WHISPER: outgoing air can carry soft words.
branches.cn: 耳语线：呼出的气可以承载轻柔的话语。

branches.en: THE LIFE: breath poured into a thing wakes it up.
branches.cn: 生命线：把气息灌进某物，就让它活起来。

branches.en: THE OUTGOING: breathing out and whispering share one stream of air.
branches.cn: 呼出线：呼气与耳语共享同一股气流。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: a whisper and a life-giving breath both move unseen air.
branches.cn: 气息线：耳语与赋予生命的气息都在推动看不见的空气。

definition_zh: 桥；桥梁、纽带；架桥、弥合；舰桥、驾驶台
definition_en: a structure built over a river or road so people can cross, something that connects two sides, or to build such a link
core_image: 横跨河面、连接两岸的石拱
scene: 河水上涨，村口那座石桥仍稳稳地跨在两岸之间。The old stone bridge still stood over the rising river.
sceneCN: 这里 bridge 是「桥」（第 1 个义项：跨越河流的建筑物）；句意为河水上涨，那座老石桥仍横跨在水面上。

pos.zh: 名词：桥；桥梁；纽带；舰桥
动词：架桥；弥合

derivatives.zh: 由 bridge 加 -able 构成，义为「可以架桥的；可以弥合的」
由 bridge 与 head 组合而成，义为「桥头堡」
由 draw 与 bridge 组合而成，义为「吊桥」

senses.title: A structure for crossing
senses.definition: a structure built over a river, road or railway so that people can cross
senses.definitionCN: 架在河流、道路或铁路上方、供人通过的建筑物
senses.example: The old stone bridge still stood over the rising river.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老石桥仍横跨在上涨的河水上。
senses.why: Old English brycg named a raised path across a stream, and that physical sense is still the first meaning.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 brycg 指横跨溪流的抬高通路，这个实体义至今仍是第一义项。

senses.title: A link between two sides
senses.definition: something that connects two groups, people or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 把两个群体、两个人或两种想法连接起来的东西
senses.example: Music became a bridge between the two families.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐成了两个家庭之间的桥梁。
senses.why: A bridge carries people from one bank to the other, so the word came to mean anything that carries understanding across a gap.
senses.whyCN: 桥把人从一岸送到另一岸，于是这个词也用来指把理解跨越空隙送过去的东西。

senses.title: To build or close a gap
senses.definition: to build a bridge over something, or to join two things that are apart
senses.definitionCN: 在某物上方架桥，或把分开的两样东西接起来
senses.example: They bridged the gap with a simple apology.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一句简单的道歉弥合了裂痕。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: putting a crossing in place, or closing a gap as if a bridge were laid over it.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：把通路架起来，或者像铺上一座桥那样把缺口接合。

senses.title: The control room of a ship
senses.definition: the raised room on a ship from which the captain controls it
senses.definitionCN: 船上供船长指挥的抬高舱室
senses.example: The captain stood on the bridge and watched the waves.
senses.exampleCN: 船长站在舰桥上望着海浪。
senses.why: The raised platform on a ship spans the vessel like a small bridge, and sailors gave it that name.
senses.whyCN: 船上抬高的平台像一座小桥横跨船体，水手便给了它这个名称。

intro.en: Bridge is an old Germanic word for a raised crossing, and its meaning has spread to links and ship decks.
intro.cn: bridge 是日耳曼语中表示「抬高通路」的古老词，词义扩展到纽带与船上的平台。

items.en: Brycg named a raised path or structure built across a stream.
items.cn: brycg 指横跨溪流建起的抬高通路或结构。

items.en: German Bruecke and Dutch brug come from the same old word.
items.cn: 德语 Bruecke 与荷兰语 brug 来自同一个古词。

items.en: The spelling became bridge, and the word kept its plain physical sense.
items.cn: 拼写变为 bridge，词义仍保持具体的实体意义。

items.en: Sailors used the word for the raised deck from which a ship is steered.
items.cn: 水手用这个词指船上操纵船只的抬高甲板。

items.en: Today a bridge can be stone or invisible, and the verb means to close a gap.
items.cn: 今天 bridge 可以是石头做的，也可以是看不见的，动词则指把缺口接合。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bridge grow from one picture: an arch that carries people from one side to the other.
sensesIntro.cn: bridge 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一道把人们从一侧送到另一侧的拱。

branches.en: THE ARCH: the structure over water is the first sense.

branches.en: THE LINK: anything that joins two sides borrows the image.

branches.en: THE DECK: a raised platform on a ship spans the vessel.

definition_zh: 明亮的；鲜艳的；聪明的；前景光明的
definition_en: full of light, strong in colour, quick to learn, or likely to succeed
core_image: 阳光直射进屋、整面窗户发亮
scene: 早晨的阳光照进教室，整面窗户亮得让人睁不开眼。Morning sun filled the classroom and the bright window hurt his eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 bright 是「明亮的」（第 1 个义项：光线充足）；句意为晨光洒进教室，明亮的窗户晃得他睁不开眼。

pos.zh: 形容词：明亮的；鲜艳的；聪明的；有希望的

derivatives.zh: 由 bright 加 -ly 构成，义为「明亮地；鲜艳地」
由 bright 加 -ness 构成，义为「明亮；亮度」

senses.title: Full of light
senses.definition: giving out or reflecting a lot of light
senses.definitionCN: 发出或反射大量光线的
senses.example: The bright window hurt his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 明亮的窗户晃得他睁不开眼。
senses.why: Old English beorht meant shining, and light is the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 beorht 意为「发亮的」，光线是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Strong in colour
senses.definition: strong and easy to see, said of colours
senses.definitionCN: 颜色浓烈醒目、容易看见
senses.example: She wore a bright red coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件鲜红的外套。
senses.why: A strong colour reflects more light, so the sense of shining spread from light to colour.
senses.whyCN: 浓烈的颜色反射更多光线，于是「发亮」的意思从光扩展到了颜色。

senses.title: Quick to learn
senses.definition: quick to learn and understand things
senses.definitionCN: 学得快、理解得快的
senses.example: He is a bright student who learns fast.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个学得很快的聪明学生。
senses.why: A bright mind was pictured as a lit room, where ideas can be seen clearly.
senses.whyCN: 聪明的头脑被想象成一间点亮的屋子，里面的想法清晰可见。

senses.title: Likely to succeed
senses.definition: full of promise, likely to be good
senses.definitionCN: 充满希望、很可能变好的
senses.example: The team has a bright future.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队前途光明。
senses.why: A good future is pictured as a lit road ahead, in contrast with a dark one.
senses.whyCN: 美好的未来被想象成前方一条明亮的道路，与昏暗的路形成对照。

sensesIntro.cn: bright 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一束让万物清晰可见的强光。

definition_zh: 带来；带（人）来；引起、导致；使达到（某状态）
definition_en: to carry something or someone to the place where the speaker is, to cause something to happen, or to make something reach a state
core_image: 手里提着东西、朝你走过来的人
scene: 妹妹从厨房端着一盘水果，走到客厅放到桌上。My sister brought a plate of fruit to the living room.
sceneCN: 这里 bring 是「带来」（第 1 个义项：把东西带到说话者所在的地方）；句意为我妹妹把一盘水果端到了客厅。

pos.zh: 动词：带来；带（人）来；引起；使达到

derivatives.zh: 由 bring 加 -er 构成，义为「带来者；送来的人」
由 up 与 bringing 组合而成，义为「抚养；教养」

senses.title: To carry something here
senses.definition: to carry or take something to the place where the speaker is
senses.definitionCN: 把东西搬到说话者所在的地方
senses.example: My sister brought a plate of fruit to the living room.
senses.exampleCN: 我妹妹把一盘水果端到了客厅。
senses.why: Old English bringan meant to carry something along, and the direction toward the speaker is built into the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bringan 意为把东西一路搬来，朝说话者所在方向的意思已经包含在词里。

senses.title: To take a person along
senses.definition: to take someone with you to a place
senses.definitionCN: 把某人一起带到某个地方
senses.example: He brought a friend to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他带了一位朋友来参加聚会。
senses.why: The same carrying motion applies to people, who are led along instead of lifted.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「带过来」的动作也适用于人，只不过人是被领着走，而不是被提起来。

senses.title: To cause something to happen
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生或出现
senses.example: The new road brought many visitors to the town.
senses.exampleCN: 新公路给小镇带来了许多游客。
senses.why: What is carried in arrives as a result, so the word came to mean producing an effect.
senses.whyCN: 被带进来的东西会带来结果，于是这个词也引申为产生某种影响。

senses.title: To make something reach a state
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to reach a particular state
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物达到某种特定状态
senses.example: The rain brought the game to an end.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨使比赛提前结束了。
senses.why: A thing is carried all the way to a new state, as if that state were a destination.
senses.whyCN: 某物被一路带到新的状态，仿佛那个状态就是一个目的地。

definition_zh: 兄弟；哥哥；弟弟；教友、修士；伙伴

core_image: 同一屋檐下一起长大的两个男孩
scene: 院子里兄弟俩共用一辆旧自行车，轮流骑着去买菜。The two brothers shared an old bike and took turns going to the market.
sceneCN: 这里 brother 是「兄弟」（第 1 个义项：同父母的男孩或男子）；句意为兄弟俩共用一辆旧自行车，轮流骑去买菜。

senses.title: A son of the same parents
senses.definition: a boy or man who has the same parents as another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人有相同父母的男孩或男子
senses.example: The two brothers shared an old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 兄弟俩共用一辆旧自行车。
senses.why: Old English brothor named a son of the same parents, and that family sense is the oldest one.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 brothor 指同父母的儿子，这个家庭义是最古老的义项。

senses.title: A member of a religious group
senses.definition: a man who belongs to a religious order or group
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个修会或宗教团体的男子
senses.example: The brothers prayed together at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们一起在黎明祈祷。
senses.why: A religious community calls its members brothers because they live and work as one family.
senses.whyCN: 宗教团体把成员称作兄弟，因为他们像一家人那样一起生活与工作。

senses.title: A close comrade
senses.definition: a man who is close to you through work, belief or shared struggle
senses.definitionCN: 因工作、信仰或共同经历而与你亲近的男子
senses.example: The soldiers called each other brother.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们彼此以兄弟相称。

entries.definition: The child of your aunt or uncle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堂（表）兄弟姐妹」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English brothor named a son of the same parents, and that is sense one.
normal.cn: 古英语 brothor 指同父母的儿子，这就是第一个义项。

normal.en: Religious groups call members brothers because they live as one family.
normal.cn: 宗教团体把成员称作兄弟，因为他们像一家人那样生活。

normal.en: The family word moved outward, so soldiers can call each other brother.
normal.cn: 这个家庭称谓向外扩展，所以士兵可以彼此称兄弟。

normal.en: It often pairs with elder, younger, big and sister.
normal.cn: 它常与 elder、younger、big、sister 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-o-t-h-e-r; the th is soft, as in mother.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-o-t-h-e-r，其中 th 读柔音，与 mother 相同。

abstract.en: See two boys sharing one bike at a gate: they are brothers.
abstract.cn: 想象两个男孩在门口共用一辆自行车：他们是兄弟。

abstract.en: Add more people who stand by one another and the same word covers a whole group.
abstract.cn: 再加入更多彼此扶持的人，同一个词就能覆盖整个群体。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the shared bike bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那辆共用的自行车把意思带回来。

examples.en: The two brothers shared an old bike.
examples.cn: 兄弟俩共用一辆旧自行车。

examples.en: The brothers prayed together at dawn.
examples.cn: 修士们一起在黎明祈祷。

examples.en: The soldiers called each other brother.
examples.cn: 士兵们彼此以兄弟相称。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「布拉泽」——同一屋檐下一起长大的男孩：兄弟

root: brother 是英语中最古老的亲属词之一，可上溯到一个意为「兄弟」的古老词根，古英语写作 brothor，与德语 Bruder、荷兰语 broeder 同源。它最初指同父母的儿子；宗教团体用这个词称呼像家人一样生活的成员；随后它又向外扩展，用来称呼任何彼此扶持的群体成员。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of brother grow from one picture: two boys growing up under one roof.
sensesIntro.cn: brother 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：两个男孩在同一屋檐下长大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two boys growing up under one roof
core.cn: 核心意象：同一屋檐下一起长大的两个男孩

branches.en: THE FAMILY: a son of the same parents is the first sense.
branches.cn: 家庭线：同父母的儿子是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE ORDER: a religious member lives as family.
branches.cn: 修会线：宗教团体的成员像家人一样生活。

branches.en: THE COMRADE: any close group can use the family word.
branches.cn: 伙伴线：任何关系紧密的群体都能使用这个家庭称谓。

branches.en: THE HOUSE: family and religious community both share one household.
branches.cn: 同屋线：家庭与宗教团体共享同一个家。

branches.en: THE BOND: faith and shared struggle both make people stand together.
branches.cn: 纽带线：信仰与共同经历都让人彼此扶持。

intro.en: Brother is a base noun, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: brother 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin frater means brother; it is a parallel word, not the source of brother.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frater 意为「兄弟」，它是平行词，不是 brother 的来源。

items.meaning: a son of the same parents
items.example: Brothor is the recorded Old English form.
items.exampleCN: brothor 是有记录的古英语形式。
